name: The Road In
description: Two very different kinds of check for one scene. The flourish is pure texture and never costs anything on any result. The trap is this chapter's first Encyclopaedia check (design/encyclopaedia-checks.md) -- background information, offered freely, wrong-but-plausible on a bad roll rather than actually punishing.

dc.basis: level 1 DC 15, one step easy — this is a treat, not a test

outcomes.criticalSuccess: It's genuinely cool, and somebody in the queue notices.
outcomes.failure: A small, funny stumble — a dropped kickstand, the wrong door, nothing that matters.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Comically embarrassing, entirely harmless — it stalls right in front of everyone.

checks.name: What that wire trap on the fence is for

outcomes.criticalSuccess: A snare, sized for something small and quick — and set with real care. Whoever placed it knew exactly what they were catching, and wanted it caught alive.
outcomes.success: A snare, sized for something small. Vermin control, probably, same as the rat traps twenty feet along.
outcomes.failure: Looks like a rat trap. Is a rat trap, as far as anyone can tell without a closer look.
outcomes.criticalFailure: They call it a rat trap with total confidence. It is not a rat trap. Nobody corrects them, because nobody else looked closely enough to know better.

notes: the-trap-on-the-fence is mystery-ledger plant #1 for the mitflit trail (design/induction.md) -- the first thing any of them ever sees of a mitflit, and it should read as absolutely nothing whether or not anyone rolls. a-flourish is never mandatory and never worth offering more than once per player; if nobody wants it, the scene loses nothing.
